name: Morgan Stanley
seo_title: Morgan Stanley assessment centre and Superday guide
description: What Morgan Stanley's own careers pages say about applying, online tests and interviews, each line linked to its source.
intro: This guide sums up what Morgan Stanley's own careers pages say about applying and interviewing, from how to apply to how Morgan Stanley suggests you prepare. It reflects those pages as we checked them on 16 October 2026. Processes differ by programme, role and country, so check Morgan Stanley's careers site for your role before you apply.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's careers contact page asks applicants to complete its online application, and lists graduaterecruitmenteurope@morganstanley.com as the general recruiting email for its EMEA headquarters in London.
For its 2027 Investment Banking Summer Analyst Programme in London, Morgan Stanley says it recruits on a rolling basis and encourages people to apply as soon as possible.
For the same London programme, Morgan Stanley says applicants should be in their penultimate year of study, graduating in 2028 from a bachelor's or master's degree.

For its 2027 Sales & Trading Summer Analyst Programme in London, Morgan Stanley says applicants must give accurate details, including an up-to-date CV and cover letter, because it cannot promise that applications can be edited after submission.

For the same Sales & Trading programme, Morgan Stanley says applicants can come from any degree discipline and should be on track for a 2:1 or equivalent, and that a financial degree is not essential but applicants should have a strong aptitude for numbers.

Morgan Stanley's applicant privacy notice says it uses artificial intelligence and machine learning on applications to create match scores that help recruiters filter candidates, and that its staff review these scores before making employment decisions.

Morgan Stanley says it will not ask candidates to pay money at any point in the hiring process, apart from reimbursable travel expenses, and that it does not currently use video chat rooms such as Google Hangouts for interviews.
For its 2027 Quantitative Finance Off-Cycle Internship in London, Morgan Stanley says applicants may be asked to complete a coding assessment and will be told if this applies to them.

For its 2027 Institutional Equity Division Early Careers Program in Hong Kong and Singapore, Morgan Stanley says the process typically runs from CV submission to an on-demand video interview and then final interviews, though it may vary by location.
For its 2027 Investment Management Full-time Analyst Program (Fixed Income High Yield) in Boston, Morgan Stanley says an application is not complete until the HireVue is submitted.
Morgan Stanley says it uses interviews to learn who candidates are and what motivates them, and to see whether they understand its business and what the job involves.
Morgan Stanley says its interviews could be competency-based, strengths-based, skills-based or technical.
Morgan Stanley says it does not always expect candidates to have the right answer in an interview, and is interested in how they work through a scenario.
In its article on interview mistakes, Morgan Stanley's senior interviewers say they will always ask whether the candidate has any questions.
The same article names 'Tell me about yourself', 'Why our firm' and 'Why this position?' as standard questions that candidates should have answers ready for.
For its 2027 Investment Banking Summer Analyst Programme in London, Morgan Stanley says all assessment centres will be held in London.

For its 2027 Investment Banking Summer Associate (MBA) Program in Hong Kong, Singapore and Sydney, Morgan Stanley says the process typically follows CV screening, an on-demand video interview, a Zoom interview and a Superday, though it may vary by location.
For its London Investment Banking Summer Analyst Programme, Morgan Stanley asks for strong analytical and numerical skills and the ability to explain complex ideas simply and summarise them well.
Morgan Stanley says candidates should have a convincing reason for wanting to work in the industry, at the firm and in the division they are interested in.

sections.heading: How Morgan Stanley suggests you prepare

items.text: Morgan Stanley advises candidates to know their CV well enough to explain everything on it without reading it.
Morgan Stanley suggests researching its history, capabilities, core values, structure and senior leaders, following financial news, and researching the programme and division applied to.
Morgan Stanley says it does not expect candidates to understand every area of markets, finance and economics, and suggests choosing one or two areas to discuss with knowledge and conviction.
Morgan Stanley recommends practising in front of a mirror or with another person, while avoiding sounding too rehearsed.

In its article on interview mistakes, Morgan Stanley says the biggest and most common mistake is not researching the job or division, and that investment banking candidates should know the firm's recent deals.
In a 2020 article on video interviews, Morgan Stanley advises speaking from memory rather than reading from notes, and practising several times before submitting a recorded interview.

practice_advice: Practise explaining a client situation and your recommendation out loud in a few minutes, with the answer first and then your reasons.
Keep a short list of business stories you have followed, and practise saying what each one means for a company and its bank.
Do short, timed mental maths drills most days: the numbers in a case study are easier when the arithmetic is automatic.
